title: Biochemical Isolation of Endosomal Membranes in HeLa Cells
author: Da Graça, Morel
materials: It is recommended to culture a large number of cells (from 4x107 to 6 x 107 in total) before initiating the isolation steps. Adequate starting material is essential for obtaining reproducible yields of both the ER–endosome contact site–enriched fraction and the corresponding endosome-only fraction.1.HeLa cells are cultured in MEM, supplemented with GlutaMAX (41090093; Thermo Fisher Scientific), 10% FCS, and non-essential amino acid mix (11140035; Gibco, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and incubated at 37°C with 5% CO2.2.Grow cells in 150-mm dishes, ensuring that they remain as a uniform monolayer throughout culture. For each condition, prepare at least 4 × 107 cells to obtain sufficient material for a robust purification yield. In general, the larger the starting cell mass is, the more efficient and reproducible the isolation of ER–endosome contact site–enriched fractions will be.

steps.title: Pre‑cool reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Place all buffers, reagents, tubes, rotors, centrifuge holders and the ultracentrifuge rotor on ice or in a 4 °C refrigerator. Prepare a large bucket of ice and keep 15‑mL and 1.5‑mL collection tubes, rubber adapters and syringes on ice throughout the workflow.

steps.title: Culture HeLa cells to required density
steps.instruction: Grow HeLa cells in MEM supplemented with GlutaMAX (Thermo Fisher 41090093), 10 % fetal calf serum, and non‑essential amino acid mix (Gibco 11140035) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in 150‑mm dishes. Harvest enough cells to obtain 4 × 10⁷–6 × 10⁷ total cells (minimum 4 × 10⁷ per condition).

steps.title: Prepare buffers and sucrose solutions
steps.instruction: Make 3 mM imidazole pH 7.4, HB‑EGTA buffer, 35 % sucrose, 62 % sucrose, Percoll basal medium and a fresh 30 % Percoll solution. Keep all solutions at 4 °C. Ensure EGTA is present in every buffer to maintain Ca²⁺‑free conditions.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Place each culture dish on ice, discard media and wash twice with 5 mL cold PBS. Add 6 mL cold PBS to the dish and gently scrape cells in a circular motion with a cold cell scraper (≤2 min per dish). Collect the cell suspension with a wide‑bore plastic Pasteur pipette into pre‑chilled 15‑mL tubes.

steps.title: Centrifuge cells and resuspend in HB‑EGTA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 125 × g for 5 min at 4 °C (≈800 rpm). Remove the supernatant and add 3 mL HB‑EGTA buffer. Gently resuspend the pellet with a wide‑bore pipette (≤2 gentle up‑and‑down motions). Optionally pool identical samples, then centrifuge at 750 × g for 10 min at 4 °C (≈2 000 rpm).

steps.title: Lyse cells and assess homogenization
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and add an equal volume of HB‑EGTA (aim for a 1:1 ratio; use at least 200 µL). Homogenize by 1–5 gentle aspiration‑dispense cycles with a 1 000 µL wide‑bore tip, then pass the suspension through a pre‑chilled 22 G needle up to 3 slow strokes (30–60 s total). Prepare a microscopy slide with DABCO‑pen circles, place 80 µL HB‑EGTA drops, add 5 µL homogenate and examine under an inverted tissue‑culture microscope. Acceptable lysis shows round nuclei free of attached organelles; if nuclei are swollen or still surrounded by plasma membrane, restart from the harvest step.

steps.title: Clarify lysate and collect post‑nuclear supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 750 × g for 10 min at 4 °C (≈2 000 rpm). Two phases appear: a light white slightly opaque upper layer (post‑nuclear supernatant, PNS) and a viscous opaque pellet (nuclei). Collect the upper layer (PNS#1) with a cut 1 000 µL tip. Resuspend the pellet in 80 µL HB‑EDTA (≤10 pipette motions). Centrifuge this suspension at 1 180 g for 10 min at 4 °C (2 500 rpm) and collect the upper phase (PNS#2). Pool PNS#1 and PNS#2.

steps.title: Adjust PNS to 40.6 % sucrose
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 62 % sucrose to the pooled PNS to reach a final sucrose concentration of 40.6 %. Mix gently with a cut 1 000 µL tip until fully dissolved (several minutes); do not vortex. Verify sucrose concentration with a refractometer (acceptable 39–42 %, optimal 40.6 %). Keep an aliquot for later western‑blot detection.

steps.title: First ultracentrifugation to isolate light membranes
steps.instruction: In precooled TLS‑55 tubes, layer <500 µL (generally 300 µL) of the 40.6 % PNS, then gently add 500 µL of 35 % sucrose followed by 500 µL of HB‑EGTA using a 26 G needle (three distinct phases must be visible). Centrifuge at 150 000 g for 1 h at 4 °C (50 000 rpm, Optima MAX‑XP). Immediately after spin, remove the fatty surface layer, then aspirate 150 µL of the first white interface (light membranes) with a cut 200 µL tip and transfer to a fresh tube. (Optional: collect the heavy‑membrane fraction after removing the intermediate sucrose.)

steps.title: Dilute light membranes with imidazole
steps.instruction: Add 450 µL of 3 mM imidazole (pH 7.4) to the 150 µL light‑membrane fraction (3:1 imidazole:light‑membrane ratio). Mix gently with a cut 1 000 µL tip until homogeneous; avoid vortexing.

steps.title: Second ultracentrifugation to isolate EERCS
steps.instruction: In a precooled TLS‑55 tube, gently layer 1 mL of 30 % Percoll, then carefully add the 450 µL diluted light‑membrane mixture on top (the layers must remain sharp). Centrifuge at 95 000 g for 30 min at 4 °C (38 000 rpm, Optima MAX‑XP). After spin, a distinct white band (EERCS) appears at the interface.

steps.title: Collect EERCS and raw endosomal fractions
steps.instruction: Mark the position of the EERCS band. Remove a small volume from the top of the gradient to facilitate collection. Using a cut 1 000 µL tip, aspirate 300 µL of the first white interface (EERCS). Remove an additional 100 µL to prevent cross‑contamination. Then collect the next 300 µL (raw endosomal population) strictly by volume (the fraction is not visible).

steps.title: Prepare samples for western blot
steps.instruction: Dilute each collected fraction to 1× Laemmli buffer containing 25 mM DTT. Heat the samples for 5 min at 95 °C and proceed with SDS‑PAGE and western‑blot analysis.

description: This protocol describes the isolation and purification of total endosomal membranes associated with endoplasmic reticulum (ER) membranes, called EERCS for endosome-ER contact sites, from mammalian cells using subcellular fractionation and density-gradient centrifugations. These steps are then followed by validation of EERCS enrichment using biochemical approach. Membrane contact sites between organelles are dynamic and transient structures2,3,4 that are difficult to isolate biochemically. While protocols for isolating ER-mitochondria contact sites have been established for many years,5 comparable approaches for other contact sites, including ER-endosome interfaces, remain limited. The present protocol describes the specific steps used to isolate EERCS fractions from HeLa cells, developed in Da Graça et al.1 However, this workflow can also be applied to other mammalian cell lines (e.g., HEK293 or MEFs) after optimization of homogenization conditions and provided that you start from a large quantity of material. Using this protocol, you will isolate an ER–endosome contact site (EERCS)–enriched fraction containing both ER-resident tethering proteins (e.g., VAPs, VMP1, KTN1) and endosomal markers (e.g., RAB GTPases, EEA1). This fraction can be directly compared, in a volume-to-volume manner, with a companion fraction enriched exclusively in endosomal proteins that are not engaged in ER contact. Together, these two fractions allow quantitative assessment of the proportion of endosomes physically associated with the ER under a given condition. In our previous study,1 this fractionation strategy enabled the quantification of dynamic changes in ER–endosome contacts across distinct endosomal subpopulations during cellular stress responses. The protocol is therefore well suited for interrogating how membrane contact sites reorganize in response to physiological or experimental perturbations.
